summary: Follow-up bridge to close Skyline escalation. Reviewed root cause hypotheses (KV cache eviction + bursty prefix cache pressure), validated mitigations deployed (fallback routing, larger KV cache pool config on Dedicated), agreed on extra hardening steps and comms. Customer asked for postmortem doc, runbook changes, and a replay test. Next steps and owners assigned.
topics: Root cause hypotheses: KV cache + prefix caching
Mitigations deployed: fallback routing, autoscale tweaks
Security/audit questions: SSO, audit logs, KMS
Next steps: postmortem, replay tests, runbook updates
Discussion of Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-11
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Alex Rivera (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Liu (Skyline Eng Lead), Maria Gonzales (Skyline SRE), Tom Baxter (Skyline CTO)

00:00 Alex Rivera: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the postmortem items and make sure the ops escalation is closed on your side. is this still a good time?
00:12 Jordan Liu: Yeah works for me, sorry been in back-to-back. we'll do a quick recap from skyline then open it up for questions.
00:18 Maria Gonzales: quick note, we did see one more 503 on auth last night about 01:30 UTC but it was transient, not a full blowout.
00:25 Alex Rivera: Right, and that was after we pushed the fallback route change and increased the kv cache pool. that seemed to catch things.
00:33 Priya Patel: Just to be explicit, the root cause we believe is twofold: an eviction storm in the KV cache combined with a sudden prefix cache miss pattern from a batch job which caused token generation latency to spike. some of the telemetry was a little noisy.
00:50 Tom Baxter: eviction storm meaning the K V cash evicting hot entries? we usually have a TTL of 6 hours not minutes.
00:58 Priya Patel: yeah, exactly. there was an ordering bug in our prefetch heuristic that interacted poorly with your workload — it caused a short window where hot entries were evicted and then re-populated in a thundering-herd pattern. that increased CPU on the inference nodes.
01:18 Jordan Liu: just to check: this is on Dedicated yes? or was part of the workred routed to hosted?
01:25 Alex Rivera: this was on Dedicated capacity in your us-west-2 pool, the Dedicated cluster handled the traffic but hit higher latency; fallback routing to x-small hosted nodes prevented a complete failure.
01:38 Maria Gonzales: there was some confusion in our ops runbook about what to flip first — autoscale or fallback. that delay of ~7 minutes is what bit us.
01:48 Priya Patel: we noted that and we adjusted the runbook before the second incident — Alex pushed the updated version to the support portal.
01:56 Alex Rivera: yep, updated runbook in the portal, link in the follow-up email.
02:05 Jordan Liu: on the security side, Tom wanted confirmation we didn't leak any tokens or have unauthorized access during the event.
02:12 Tom Baxter: right, need assurance.
02:15 Priya Patel: understood. We reviewed the audit logs; we didn't see any abnormal API keys usage. note: the SSO logs were a little delayed due to your provider's retention script, but we have a copy.
02:30 Maria Gonzales: i saw S S O delays, yes. can you attach that to the postmortem?
02:34 Alex Rivera: absolutely, we'll attach the SSO and API audit slices.
02:40 Jordan Liu: can you also confirm KMS usage? we rotate keys monthly, want to make sure there was no misconfig.
02:48 Priya Patel: KMS calls look normal, no failed decrypts; we did see an increased rate but within expected thresholds. will include KMS call graph in the doc.
02:55 Alex Rivera: quick sanity question — any sign of a mem leak versus cache thrash?
03:01 Maria Gonzales: telemetry favors thrash. memory growth plateaued and dropped after the eviction window closed.
03:10 Priya Patel: and to be clear, the inference runtime picked a different kernel path under high concurrency which made CPU spiky; this is an optimization path we call "fast-path fallthrough" but it has a resource tradeoff.
03:28 Jordan Liu: is that a config toggle we can alter?
03:31 Priya Patel: yes, we can pin a conservative kernel selection and avoid the fast-path; performance drops a bit but stability improves.
03:39 Tom Baxter: good to have that option. we prefer predictable latency over occasional micro-gains.
03:46 Alex Rivera: noted, added to next steps — Priya will run a controlled test of kernel pinning in staging.
03:52 Priya Patel: i'll do that and report latency/cost delta.
04:00 Maria Gonzales: timeline question: how quickly can we get the replay test results? we want to validate the KV cache fix under load.
04:07 Priya Patel: aiming for 48-72 hours; i can run the replay this week and share raw traces.
04:12 Jordan Liu: ok. also curious about the fallback policy — during the event, some requests routed to the hosted tier and that increased egress cost. can we quantify?
04:23 Alex Rivera: yes, we've got cost delta estimates; i'll include a cost breakdown by minute and token. early rough number was about a 14% spike in unit costs during the peak.
04:35 Tom Baxter: i may need that for internal chargeback. thanks.
04:40 Maria Gonzales: we also need a change to the runbook: make fallback automatic at 95th percentile latency for two consecutive minutes, not three. the extra minute hurts.
04:51 Priya Patel: we can change that threshold; need to validate false positive risk.
04:56 Jordan Liu: what about alerts? we had a bunch of duplicate alerts. can we consolidate them?
05:01 Alex Rivera: yes, we're recommending a single composite alert on request latency plus error rate to reduce noise.
05:08 Maria Gonzales: also, can Redwood attach a short-lived synthetic job that runs prefix-access patterns so the cache pre-warms?
05:16 Priya Patel: we have a proposed prefix prewarm script; we can share, but many customers run it from their side. we can provide an example in the postmortem.
05:26 Jordan Liu: perfect.
05:29 Tom Baxter: i want to raise a governance question — Dedicated gives us isolation but made us operate the autoscaling piece. is there a hybrid mode where Redwood handles more of the scaling?
05:42 Alex Rivera: good question. we do offer a managed scaling addon for Dedicated — we can take the autoscale decision and apply conservative burst capacity. it's opt-in and has a separate SLA.
05:52 Tom Baxter: send the doc. if it reduces ops burden we may buy it.
05:58 Alex Rivera: will do.
06:04 Priya Patel: quick note on surprise behaviors: during the event our KV cache eviction metric sampling window was 10s which masked the rapid thrash. we've proposed reducing sampling to 5s for critical keys.
06:18 Maria Gonzales: that would help visibility, yes.
06:23 Jordan Liu: any indications of a security exploit?
06:26 Priya Patel: no, nothing indicates compromise; pattern looks like workload interaction. we'll include the indicators of compromise check list in the doc.
06:34 Alex Rivera: i'll attach the IOCs and the list of telemetry queries used.
06:38 Jordan Liu: great.
06:40 [crosstalk] Maria Gonzales: also want to mention our internal oncall handoff was messy, we need a clearer playbook for who toggles fallback.
06:48 Alex Rivera: agreed, the runbook will list explicit roles.
06:52 Priya Patel: action: i'll update the runbook, Alex will publish, Maria validate.
07:00 Jordan Liu: can we talk about SLA credits? in the incident window we were over SLO for 12 minutes.
07:08 Alex Rivera: we can engage billing once the postmortem is accepted; credits follow our SLA terms. I'll open an internal case.
07:16 Tom Baxter: fine.
07:20 Maria Gonzales: one more ask — please include the pre and post traces showing kernel selection. that helped our infra team understand the spike.
07:29 Priya Patel: yes, will include kernel-path heatmaps.
07:34 Alex Rivera: ok moving to closure items. quick recap of what we agreed so it's on record.
07:40 Alex Rivera: 1) postmortem doc with timeline, telemetry, IOCs, KMS/audit slices (Alex)
07:46 Alex Rivera: 2) KV cache replay on staging (Priya)
07:49 Alex Rivera: 3) runbook update and explicit fallback ownership (Priya + Maria)
07:55 Alex Rivera: 4) kernel pinning test (Priya)
07:58 Alex Rivera: 5) cost breakdown and chargeback numbers (Alex)
08:03 Jordan Liu: sounds right. can we also get a short executive summary for my CTO?
08:09 Alex Rivera: yes i'll include a one-pager.
08:12 Tom Baxter: make it clear what buy vs build options are for future preventions.
08:17 Alex Rivera: will do.
08:20 [long pause, typing]
09:05 Jordan Liu: quick phone check, who do i email if i need the raw traces sooner?
09:10 Priya Patel: ping me directly, priya@redwood.ai, i'll share the S3 link.
09:14 Alex Rivera: and cc support@redwood.com so we track it in the ticket.
09:20 Maria Gonzales: ok thanks.
09:22 Jordan Liu: any regulatory concerns? we have some european customers, want to make sure data residency is respected for the logs.
09:29 Priya Patel: logs we're sharing are access slices, no PII; for EU retention we can anonymize and provide regionally stored copies if needed.
09:39 Tom Baxter: good.
09:42 Alex Rivera: wrapping up — any blockers to closure from Skyline's side?
09:46 Jordan Liu: none, we just want the postmortem and replay results.
09:51 Maria Gonzales: agree, and i'll validate runbook changes once published.
09:55 Tom Baxter: and please include the managed scaling addon details and cost.
09:59 Alex Rivera: will include.
10:03 [transition noise]
11:12 Alex Rivera: final note: competitor question — we had an internal ask comparing behavior to GiantCloud. for context, their managed routing is more aggressive in failing over which reduces customer-side ops but costs more.
11:27 Tom Baxter: ok noted.
11:30 Alex Rivera: thanks everyone, we'll send the follow-up with links and action items.
11:34 Jordan Liu: thank you.
11:36 Maria Gonzales: thanks.
11:38 Priya Patel: thanks all.

(Transcript ends — actual meeting duration 46 minutes. Timestamps approximate because of transcription segmentation.)
